children: Blackstone Inc. (NYSE:BX) is reshaping its portfolio: it’s exiting Bumble while doubling then selling down its stake, buying Flow Control Holdings and Sanha Logistics Park II, eyeing a ~$2B ZO Skin Health sale, financing AirTrunk’s $1.6B loan for a Singapore IPO, and naming new real estate co‑heads.
: Blackstone (BX) is exiting Bumble, having doubled its stake. It plans to finish selling by early next year, using a UBS deal allowing under 5% of Bumble per quarter.
: Blackstone (BX) private equity funds will acquire Flow Control Holdings, a U.S. maker of data‑center liquid‑cooling components; terms undisclosed, Audax keeps a minority stake, deal due Q4.
: Blackstone (BX) named David Levine and Giovanni Cutaia co-heads of global real estate, overseeing a real-estate portfolio valued at over $600 billion.
: Blackstone (BX) is exploring a potential sale of ZO Skin Health, a dermatology skincare asset valued near $2 billion; the process is early and advisors Citigroup and Raymond James are involved.
: Blackstone’s data center arm AirTrunk seeks a $1.6 billion loan to back its planned Singapore IPO, financing tied specifically to the unit as it readies the offering.
: Blackstone (BX) bought a majority stake in Sanha Logistics Park II, a 334,000 m2 dry-storage logistics project near Seoul. Construction along Gyeongbu Expressway ends in 2028; cost ~600bn KRW.
